source: web-client/scripts/dump-entries.ts against a live pi session (room QlEDzdZoHZWc); same session as 011 driven to 100 entries
scrub: Every string → «length» except structural keys (id, parentId, role, toolCallId, toolName, type, model, …). Two exceptions, both deliberate: (1) a trailing pi notice matching its own template (`[… N more lines in file. Use offset=N to continue.]`) is kept, since it carries offsets not content; (2) an edit's `details.diff` / `details.patch` keep their bodies with absolute paths replaced by «path» — the diff IS the thing under test, and it targets a throwaway scratch file. `sections` keeps keys, loses values; `usage` counts zeroed. Verified: no absolute path, username, hostname or command line survives.
description: A long real session on the replay plane: 100 entries — 20+ assistant turns whose content is always [thinking, toolCall] (so the transcript is user rows plus cards, never an assistant bubble), 18+ tool results, 23 extension `custom` entries, one `system` entry. Pins: (a) `read`/`bash` results carry NO `details` at all — the face guard accepts the empty-details path, and read's truncation notice exists only in the TEXT (`[965 more lines in file. Use offset=201 to continue.]`); (b) a `bash` result ending in bracketed usage text (`… [-B blocksize] [file ...]`) that is NOT a notice — the split must key on pi's `\n\n[` seam; (c) `edit` results DO carry `details: {diff, patch, firstChangedLine}`, and the two diff fields are DIFFERENT formats — `diff` is line-number prefixed (`-1 # Heading A`), `patch` is a unified diff — the face parses `patch` (reference ToolFace.swift:193), not `diff`.
note: The dump records the walk's pages, not their boundaries: 100 entries are written as one page plus the terminal page. Paging across real page boundaries stays 009's job.
